Thermal constraint fails for every pair: the coldest maximum returned vial-bottom temperature is -32.55 C at 0.05 Torr/-25 C shelf, still 3.45 C above the -36 C limit; that pair also exceeds the whole-batch equipment line at peak (1.556 vs 0.403 kg/h). The only pair inside the equipment line is 0.2 Torr/-25 C (peak whole-batch rate 0.986 vs 2.158 kg/h), but its maximum returned vial-bottom temperature is -28.90 C, 7.10 C above T_pr_crit. 11 of 12 pairs exceed the line at peak (whole-batch peak = returned maximum flux x 5.024 m2). No allowed pair satisfies both constraints, so no feasible recipe exists among the candidates. Maxima are over returned solver nodes with no continuous-maximum guarantee. Simulated values from the authored native model, not measurements; simulator-world task, not experimental validation.

output.content:
**Verdict: no_feasible_recipe** — none of the 12 allowed pressure/shelf pairs can complete drying while holding vial-bottom temperature at or below −36 °C and staying within the whole-batch equipment line. The assessment is saved (draft, requires review), with all 12 native simulation result_ids attached.

**Why, from the simulated runs:**

- **Thermal constraint (vial-bottom ≤ −36 °C) fails for every pair.** The coldest maximum returned vial-bottom temperature across all 12 runs is **−32.55 °C** at 0.05 Torr / −25 °C shelf — still **3.45 °C above** the limit. Hotter shelf temperatures only push it higher (up to **−17.00 °C** at 0.2 Torr / +10 °C).
- **Equipment line (−0.182 + 11.7·P_Torr kg/h) fails for 11 of 12 pairs.** Peak whole-batch sublimation rate = returned maximum flux × 5.024 m² (16,000 vials × 3.14 cm² each). Example at 0.05 Torr: peak 0.310 kg/h/m² × 5.024 m² = **1.556 kg/h** vs a line capacity of 0.403 kg/h — nearly 4× over.
- The **only** pair inside the equipment line is 0.2 Torr / −25 °C (peak 0.986 vs 2.158 kg/h), but its maximum returned vial-bottom temperature is −28.90 °C, **7.10 °C above** the thermal limit.
- Since thermal feasibility fails everywhere, predicted drying time (ranging from ~6.0 h at 0.2 Torr/+10 °C to ~34.6 h at 0.2 Torr/−25 °C) is moot; no constraint margins are reported because no recipe is feasible.

**Caveats I could not check or verify:**
- These are **simulator-world outputs from the authored LyoPRONTO model**, not measurements and not experimental validation.
- Maxima are taken over returned solver nodes only — the source explicitly notes **no continuous-maximum guarantee**, so a true peak between nodes could exceed what's reported here.
- I did not use internal process models, per your instruction.
- This is a saved draft assessment, not an approval or manufacturing action.
